events.description: The Sigurd Frosterus collection of early modern art is on display in the Frosterus Hall at Amos Rex. Featuring some of the Sigurd Frosterus Foundation Collection’s most important works from the early twentieth century, the presentation brings out the vibrancy and colour intensity of the paintings. Two painters who stand out in particular are Magnus Enckell and Alfred William Finch, both represented by more than ten works. title.en: The Ghost and the Invention Device

summary.en: The exhibition tells a story about the Ghost of the Museum.

ai.en: An interactive exhibition for children aged 5 to 9 at the Museum of Technology, where they learn about inventions through play and tasks, then switch on the Ghost's Invention Device.

events.description: The exhibition tells a story about the Ghost of the Museum. The Ghost requests children to learn about technology via play, mysteries, hands-on tasks and inventing. The exhibition includes different areas with different viewpoints into technology: essence of technology, stages of invention, values and relevance of technology, collaboration, Finnish inventions and changes that have taken place in technology in the long run. As a culmination of the museum tour children can switch on The Ghost’s Invention Device by using the new skills they have learned in the exhibition. The Ghost and the Invention Device is an interactive and child-centered learning environment that includes versatile learning methods. The environment together with museum objects support children’s creative museum engagement and encourages them to observe, handle and understand technology as a part of their everyday life. Museum of Technology 10.9.2016-31.12.2027 For children of 5 to 9 yrs

summary.en: The heart of the Sinebrychoff Art Museum is the unique home of Paul and Fanny Sinebrychoff, which has been on permanent display

ai.en: The Sinebrychoff family's historic town house, on permanent display at the Sinebrychoff Art Museum. Entry is free.

events.description: The heart of the Sinebrychoff Art Museum is the unique home of Paul and Fanny Sinebrychoff, which has been on permanent display on the second floor of the building since 27 November 1921. The Sinebrychoffs’ palatial town house at Bulevardi 40 was completed in 1842. The building was immediately considered to be one of the most significant private homes in Helsinki. The last occupants of the house bearing the name Sinebrychoff, Paul and Fanny Sinebrychoff, were passionate art enthusiasts. They collected the most beautiful European art and objects for their home. When their collections were donated to the Finnish state in 1921, they comprised more than 900 items. Paul and Fanny’s wish to open the doors of their home to the public to see the art treasures they had collected was recorded in a will almost one hundred years ago. The same spirit still lives on in the museum. Sinebrychoff Art Museum 27.11.2021-31.1.2040 Free entry

title.en: Tove Jansson Gallery: Artist Family Jansson

summary.en: The Tove Jansson Gallery at HAM opens on a larger scale than ever before, now spreading across three exhibition halls.

ai.en: The Tove Jansson Gallery at HAM, across three halls, with its first show on the Jansson family of artists. It marks 80 years of "Comet in Moominland".

events.description: The Tove Jansson Gallery at HAM opens on a larger scale than ever before, now spreading across three exhibition halls. The Tove Jansson Gallery is built around the beloved frescos Party in the Countryside and Party in the City, which are permanently on display. Spanning three exhibition halls, the gallery aims to strengthen Tove Jansson’s artistic legacy and significance in both art history and Finnish society. It showcases Jansson’s art in a diverse way and introduces new perspectives on her as both a Helsinki-based and international artist. The gallery’s first exhibition presents the diverse forms of expression and shared artistic projects of the Jansson family of artists. Photographs also provide a glimpse into the family’s leisure time. The home’s atmosphere, close relationships and shared family adventures were later reflected in the Moomin stories that launched Tove Jansson to international fame. The Artist Family Jansson exhibition commemorates the book Comet in Moominland, which is celebrating its 80th anniversary in 2026. Helsinki Art Museum HAM 13.2.2026-10.1.2027 Admission fee 0-20€

title.en: Anna Sinebrychoff - Ahead of Her Time

summary.en: Anna Sinebrychoff (1830–1904) had a bourgeois girl’s education, married the successful businessman Paul Sinebrychoff (1799–1883) in 1850.

ai.en: A display on Anna Sinebrychoff, a 19th-century Helsinki businesswoman who led her family's brewery and was known for her charity work.

events.description: Anna Sinebrychoff (1830–1904) had a bourgeois girl’s education, married the successful businessman Paul Sinebrychoff (1799–1883) in 1850, and they had four children. On her husband’s death, she attained a position that was rare for a woman in Finland, as majority shareholder and chair of the board of a large company. In the latter half of the 19th century, she became the most important woman in the prominent Sinebrychoff Brewery clan. She resolutely led the family and kept a close eye on the work of her two sons as they managed the company. She was the undisputed matriarch and a revered grandmother. Anna Sinebrychoff died in 1904. The numerous obituaries noted her extensive charitable work. The exhibition offers a broad overview of Anna’s life and work in Helsinki from the 1850s onwards. At its core is Anna Sinebrychoff the active influencer: bearer of responsibility for the family and business, benefactor, prominent figure in associations and societies, and member of the Orthodox congregation. Sinebrychoff Art Museum, Red Cellar 3.3.2026-29.8.2027 Tue, Thu, Fri 11.00-18.00 Wed 10.00-20.00 Sat-Sun 10.00-17.00 Admission fee 0-21€

events.description: The touring exhibition organized by the Finnish Glass Museum celebrates the inclusion of handmade glassmaking on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The exhibition presents the tradition of handmade glass and highlights Finnish glassmaking activities and expertise. Glass has been blown in Suomenlinna since the 1970s. The studio glass activity initiated by Heikki Kallio has been continued by Glass Studio Hytti, which has hosted several makers of both functional and art glass. The touring exhibition has been complemented with works by Heikki Kallio and glass artists who have worked in Suomenlinna in the 2020s. Suomenlinna Museum 6.3.2026-10.1.2027 Daily 10.30-17.00; June-August 10.00-18.00 Admission fee 5-10€

title.en: Paper Stars – Paper Dolls by Rauni Palonen

summary.en: Paper Stars – Paper Dolls by Rauni Palonen, 1968–1982

ai.en: A small exhibition at Tamminiemi of paper dolls by Rauni Palonen, drawn for Apu magazine from 1968 to 1982, showing celebrities of the Kekkonen era.

events.description: Paper Stars – Paper Dolls by Rauni Palonen, 1968–1982 Tamminiemi features a nostalgic glimpse into the world of celebrities and popular culture of President Kekkonen’s era. The small-scale exhibition showcases paper dolls drawn by fashion artist and editor Rauni Palonen (b. 1929). Originally published in Apu magazine between 1968 and 1982, these drawings depicted the most celebrated stars of the era: beauty queens, singers, actors, television personalities, athletes, and even royalty from neighbouring countries. Palonen would produce weekly sketches of celebrities, complete with outfits tailored to the latest fashion trends. For many, these paper stars were treasured toys. They were carefully cut out, glued to cardboard, accessorised with handmade outfits, and preserved with care. Several of these paper stars were also a familiar sight at Kekkonen’s home in Tamminiemi or at the Independence Day reception at the Presidential Palace. Paper Stars is a tribute to the long and distinguished career of fashion editor Rauni Palonen, whose paper dolls were known to the entire nation in her time. The collection donated by Palonen to the Finnish Heritage Agency’s Picture Collections contains a total of 207 paper stars. In this small-scale exhibition, approximately 80 figures are on display, featuring both digitised versions and original drawings. Tamminiemi 17.4.2026-9.1.2028

summary.en: How does a bee perceive the world? What would disappear from the dining table without pollinators? The world of pollinators comes to life!

ai.en: An exhibition on pollinators at the Natural History Museum, with interactive games, bingo and specimens. It is based on a non-fiction book.

events.description: The world of pollinators comes to life! How does a bee perceive the world? What would disappear from our dining table without pollinators? And did you know that mosquitoes, wasps, and even snails also pollinate flowers? The exhibition offers fascinating information about pollinators, stunning visuals, and engaging activities. Visitors can play the interactive "Identify the Pollinators" game and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the Natural History Museum's remarkable specimens. The exhibition is based on the non-fiction book Pölyttäjien kirjo by Mia Rönkä and Janne Toriseva. Natural History Museum 20.5.2026-6.6.2027

summary.en: The exhibition invites visitors to explore Alvar,  Aino and Elissa Aalto’s architecture and design from the perspective of wellbeing.

ai.en: An exhibition on the Aaltos' architecture and design through the lens of wellbeing, with drawings, furniture and a calm Aalto Lounge.

events.description: The exhibition invites visitors to explore Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto’s architecture and design from the perspective of wellbeing. The exhibition highlights wellbeing as the Aaltos’ major contribution to Western architectural modernism and examines how their work and philosophy approach it as a balance between people, nature, the built environment, and materials. It connects the Aaltos’ idea of holistic wellbeing with contemporary thinking and the growing desire to understand wellbeing as extending beyond the individual to concern the whole planet. The exhibition brings together a diverse dialogue of presentation methods and materials, including drawings and scale models, furniture, glass objects and material experiments, as well as artworks. The exhibition also features rarely displayed items from the museum’s collections. Among other works, the exhibition includes the multi-channel video installation Other Actors (2025) by London-based artist and researcher Ilona Sagar. The Aalto Lounge offers a calm space for rest and reflection and invites visitors to explore how being in a space affects their body and mind in the presence of authentic Aalto objects. Architecture and Design Museum 5.6.2026-6.1.2027 Admission fee 0-23€ Further information about the exhibition and public program will be announced at a later date.

summary.en:
Tarinoita pelon ja toivon vuosikymmeniltä:
Esa Leskisen Toinen tasavalta kertoo Suomen ponnisteluista säilyttää demokraattinen valtiomuotonsa.

ai.en: "Toinen tasavalta" at the National Theatre's Main Stage, a 2026 play on Finland's postwar years, with Urho Kekkonen at its centre. It is in Finnish and runs 2 hours 45 minutes.

events.description: Tarinoita pelon ja toivon vuosikymmeniltä Esa Leskisen Toinen tasavalta kertoo Suomen ponnisteluista säilyttää demokraattinen valtiomuotonsa Neuvostoliiton painostuksen, kansainvälisten konfliktien ja sisäisten poliittisten ristiriitojen puristuksessa. Esitys on Leskisen demokratia-aiheisen esityssarjan itsenäinen neljäs osa, jonka edeltäjä oli huippusuosittu Ensimmäinen tasavalta (2022). Toinen tasavalta on älykäs, viihdyttävä ja elävän ajankuvan värittämä esitys, joka vyöryttää kansalliselle päänäyttämölle historian äkkikäänteitä ja henkilöitä sodanjälkeisistä vaaran vuosista 1980-luvun juppiaikaan ja neuvostoimperiumin romahdukseen. Se on tarina kansakunnasta, joka vastoin kaikkia todennäköisyyksiä kykeni torjumaan itseensä kohdistuneet uhat, sopimaan keskinäiset riitansa ja samalla rakentamaan tasa-arvoisen, kaikki kansalaiset huomioon ottavan hyvinvointiyhteiskunnan. Esityksen keskushenkilönä ja aikakautensa itseoikeutettuna symbolina toimii Urho Kekkonen. Nuoremman Kekkosen roolissa nähdään Janne Reinikainen, vanhempaa valtiomiestä esittää Vesa Vierikko. events.description: The Modern Classics series of exhibitions presents 20th-century artists from the Finnish National Gallery collections. The first artist to be featured in the series is Elga Sesemann. Elga Sesemann’s (1922–2007) life story is an exceptional and interesting example of a professional woman artist making a career for herself in Finland. The artist’s very first solo exhibition in Helsinki, in 1945, already drew the attention of critics and the art audience to her expressive style. Sesemann’s artistic oeuvre is extensive, and she enjoyed an active career, with her expression constantly evolving, until the mid-1990s. Ateneum Art Museum 18.8.2026-8.8.2027

summary.en: The concert is a synthesis of luohti, electronic music, jouhikko and video art that explores the contemporary expression of the Sámi worldview.

ai.en: An audiovisual concert at Kiasma Theatre, combining Sámi yoiks by Ánnámáret with electronic music and video. The ticket includes Kiasma's exhibitions that day.

events.description: Bálvvosbáiki is an audiovisual concert in which the Sámi yoiks (luohtis) performed by Ánnámáret intertwine with Turkka Inkilä’s nuanced electronic music, Ilkka Heinonen’s gritty and partially effected jouhikko, and Marja Viitahuhta’s video art combining animation, archival footage, and material filmed in Sápmi. The luohtis reflect how the Sámi worldview manifests in the present day, while the concert also touches on themes of colonialism and environmental awareness. Are the female deities Sáráhkka, Juhksáhkka and Uksáhkka still present? Can the power of a sieidi be experienced through yoiking? What does intergenerational sorrow feel like? The concert is part of Kiasma's We Who Remain - Sámi Art in Focus exhibition's programme. Ticket includes admission to Kiasma's exhibitions on the day of the performance.

summary.en: Creative Destruction – A photographic series by Johan Eichhorn

ai.en: Johan Eichhorn's staged photographs move forest roads and drained wetlands into domestic spaces, asking why we accept such changes in nature. At the Natural History Museum until January 2027.

events.description: Johan Eichhorn’s Creative Destruction shifts human interventions in nature into the human living environment. Instead of forest roads cutting through woodlands, drainage drying out wetlands, and dams altering waterways, these elements appear in people’s homes and other everyday spaces. In the staged photographs, familiar environments become strange. At the same time, they make visible the ways we reshape nature – changes that have gradually become an almost unnoticed part of our daily lives. The exhibition does not aim to provide answers, but invites viewers to reflect on why we accept in nature things we would never accept in our own living environment. Natural History Museum 1.9.2026-10.1.2027

summary.en: This exhibition delves into the bold and multifaceted world of the beloved artist Elin Danielson-Gambogi (1861–1919).

ai.en: An exhibition on painter Elin Danielson-Gambogi's self-portraits and her identity as a woman and artist, at the Didrichsen Art Museum until January 2027.

events.description: This exhibition delves into the bold and multifaceted world of the beloved artist Elin Danielson-Gambogi (1861–1919). Her works reveal the artist’s exploration of the roles of woman, artist, and individual at the crossroads of two cultures, and how she built her identity through art at a time when women were not yet allowed that right. Danielson’s self-portraits, intimate depictions of everyday life, and the tensions within her gazes tell a story of self-discovery and the defense of one’s own voice – themes that continue to resonate today. summary.en: The Peacock in the Garden – Mathias Withoos and Rome

ai.en: Paintings by Mathias Withoos and other members of the Bentvueghels, the Dutch and Flemish artists' group in Rome. The show runs at the Sinebrychoff Art Museum until January 2027.

events.description: The Peacock in the Garden – Mathias Withoos and Rome Like many of his colleagues, the painter Mathias Withoos joined the Bentvueghels during his stay in Rome around 1648–1653. Rome can be seen in his art in the landscapes, which he framed with abundant plant motifs. In his signature still-life paintings, undergrowth teeming with life is combined with elements from a sublime urban landscape. In his oeuvre he repeatedly returned to Roman and Italian influences. The Bentvueghels group sprang up among Dutch and Flemish artists in Rome around 1620, and the community continued in existence for a century, until 1720. They were boisterous revellers who spent time in close-knit togetherness in their new city. But being in Rome was about more than just carousing. They took art making and artistic development seriously. The members of the Bentvueghels were especially keen on drawing and painting in the open air. The artists wanted to learn from the Italian masters, and also sought out new views in the city. The group included, among others, Caspar van Wittel (1653–1736), Jan Both (1618–1652) and Cornelis van Poelenburgh (1594–1667), whose works are in this exhibition. title.en: Antti Tolvi: For Organ and Pause

summary.en: Antti Tolvi´s work consists of sound, light and beds that vibrate at a low frequency, and it invites you to pause and reflect.

ai.en: "For Organ and Pause" by Antti Tolvi, a long-running sound installation and performance with an organ and beds, open at HAM until January 2027.

events.description: Please come in, lie down and relax. For Organ and Pause is both an installation and a long-duration performance that begins when the exhibition opens and ends when it closes. Together, the sound, light and beds create a slowly evolving and transforming work of art. The continuous sound is produced by the angelica archangelica organ and beds that go quiet six times during the exhibition. These pauses provide space for the performances composed by Tolvi and performed by him together with other musicians. Tolvi is a sound artist and performer with a background in experimental music. Tolvi is fascinated by long-duration performances that challenge our perception of time. A work that goes on for more than three months is impossible to experience from start to finish. Instead, you can quieten down and pause to savour it for a specific, unique moment. Space for New Art is HAM’s new platform for versatile art-making and innovative exhibition concepts. The space offers – engaging both body and mind – captivating encounters with art and artists. The first open call focused on exhibition proposals that enliven the art experience through performative and audience-engaging methods. ai.en: "Like a Prayer", an exhibition of Emma Ainala's paintings from the past ten years, mostly of women and girls in nature or enclosed rooms, with references to pop culture and art history. It is at Kiasma.

events.description: The main characters in Emma Ainala's works are often girls and women who linger amid luxuriant nature or in enclosed interiors. Some have transformed into spiders or snakes. One bears the features of a sphinx, while others have taken on the form of a centaur. The exhibition presents Ainala’s works from the past ten years, bringing together both new paintings and key works from across her career. According to the artist, the exhibition title Like a Prayer refers both to the act of painting and to viewing artworks. In both situations, an individual is faced with something unknown. It is a moment that calls for letting go of control and trusting intuition. Ainala’s richly detailed paintings are filled with references to popular culture, fashion and art history. Through her art, she seeks to defend the multifacetedness of life: alongside limiting roles, there can also be joy and possibility. In her works, women are compared to pet animals and blend into the décor around them, yet they also glow brightly in the darkness.

title.en: Emma Talbot: You Are Not the Centre

summary.en: British artist Emma Talbot fills HAM’s grand arched hall with glowing colours, flowing patterns, and poetic handwritten texts.

ai.en: "You Are Not the Centre", a show by Emma Talbot at HAM with silk paintings, textiles and drawings, and an animation that puts humans back among other living things. It runs until April 2027.

events.description: In her art, Emma Talbot (b. 1969) explores relationships between humans and nature in an era defined by the climate crisis, biodiversity loss and technological change. The artist’s own experiences and reflections expand from the personal towards the collective, forming narratives of the present day. For Talbot, drawing forms the foundation of her artistic practice, serving both as a tool for thinking and a channel for emotions. The exhibition features large-scale silk paintings, three-dimensional textile works, as well as drawings. Together, they create a spatial installation in which the viewer can move as if following the artist’s train of thought. Talbot’s handwritten texts are an integral part of the works, opening up new perspectives on them. Also on view is the animation You Are Not the Centre, in which the narrator figure experiences the world through the senses of a dog, a spider, a bird, a deer and a moth. The animation challenges anthropocentric worldview by highlighting the intelligence and emotional capacity of the animal kingdom. In Emma Talbot’s works, humans are not placed at the centre of the world, but as part of nature and a larger whole whose pieces are interdependent. The exhibition invites to reflect on how people can collectively envision more sustainable and equitable futures. summary.en: Resting wild cats, references to various cultures, and personal messages permeate her large-scale, vibrantly coloured pieces.

events.description: Leena Luostarinen (1949–2013) ranks among Finland’s most distinguished painters, who left an indelible mark on the Finnish art world. Now presented together for the first time, the exhibitionbrings together Luostarinen’s monumental paintings from HAM’s collection, dating from what is considered her creative peak in the 1980s and 1990s. Luostarinen made her breakthrough in 1981 with a solo exhibition of large-scale feline predators. She soon became known for powerful paintings that visibly bear the marks of their making – from palette-knife traces to vigorous brushstrokes. In 1988, she was named Finland’s Artist of the Year. Despite the acclaim she received, she often felt like an outsider, sensing that she neither belonged nor could conform. She travelled widely, driven by a longing for distant places. Drawing on influences from many cultures, she developed a compelling, recognisable style that resists categorisation. The exhibition architecture draws its colour scheme from Luostarinen’s paintings, while subtly mimicking the symmetrical floor plan of an imaginary temple. Feline creatures guide the visitors through the exhibition, which is arranged neither chronologically nor thematically. events.description: Having captivated more than 2.5 million visitors worldwide, Tutankhamun – The Immersive Exhibition arrives in Finland for the first time. The award-winning exhibition takes visitors on a journey 3,400 years back in time to ancient Egypt and into the world of the young Pharaoh Tutankhamun. Visitors can explore the era of Tutankhamun, the culture of ancient Egypt and its famous treasures through historical content and highly detailed replicas produced in Egypt based on the original objects. The exhibition features three distinct digital experiences. In a large immersive space, six-metre-high 360-degree projections, music and storytelling surround visitors with the landscapes and temples of ancient Egypt. A VR experience takes visitors on a journey into the ancient Egyptian afterlife, while an interactive virtual world allows them to walk through the Valley of the Kings in 1922 and experience the story of the discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb. Before arriving in Finland, Tutankhamun – The Immersive Exhibition has toured 20 countries and has also been presented at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza. The exhibition is officially supported by the Grand Egyptian Museum and its audiovisual production has received three international Telly Awards. events.description: Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with this special site, the Kaisaniemi Botanic Garden — examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill these glasshouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation. Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel. title.en: COMING SOON: PUNK! 50 years of buzz in the streets of Helsinki

summary.en: Leather jackets and mohawks, zines and self-published albums, sweaty gigs and a DIY attitude. The ex…

ai.en: The "PUNK, 50 years of buzz in the streets of Helsinki" exhibition at Villa Hakasalmi, tracing Finnish punk from late-1970s venues to today with photographs, zines, album covers and a practice space.

events.description:
Leather jackets and mohawks, zines and self-published albums, sweaty gigs and a DIY attitude. The exhibition ‘PUNK! 50 years of buzz in the streets of Helsinki’ takes visitors to key meeting spaces from the late 1970s to the present day – from the Kill City neighbourhood to the Lepakko urban culture centre, and from the legendary second-hand record shop Oskun Divari to the Vuoritalo centre for alternative culture. You can watch the story of Finnish punk unfold through photographs, video interviews, album covers, zines, gig posters, clothing, musical instruments and other artefacts, such as a drum stool built by Pelle Miljoona himself and Maukka Perusjätkä ’s chainsaw.

Punk breaks out of the displays

Punk classics are playing on the jukebox, and you can pogo in the pit or pick up an instrument in the practice space. Through the young band Mökä , visitors get to see how punk music is made in the 2020s. The exhibition also sheds light on punk’s journey from an oppressed subculture to being part of Finnish cultural history. Punk emerged in London and New York in the mid-1970s, giving a voice to the rebellious youth. Despite opposition from the Finnish Government and youth organisations, this counter-culture also drew in Helsinki residents who had grown tired of elitist rock music. Half a century later, punk is still alive and well, living on in art, fashion and activism.

The past calls, the present answers

The exhibition has been curated by Teijo Hintikka…

title.en: Southnord Artfest: Pop-up Library: Center of Unfinished Business in collaboration with Contemporary And

summary.en: This pop-up contains books from C&'s collection curated by Ethel-Ruth Tawe.

ai.en: A pop-up reading room on colonialism, by the C& Center of Unfinished Business, at Oodi as part of Southnord Artfest. It includes books selected by Ethel-Ruth Tawe and an art reference collection from Southnord.

events.description: The C& Center of Unfinished Business is a reading room that offers an extraordinary, sometimes disconcerting selection of books connected to the topic of colonialism in various ways – from German colonization to Congolese fashion to twenty-first-century capital markets, it stretches into many different areas affected. Launched in 2017, the reading room has travelled and connected in various ways with institutions from Cincinnati to Hong Kong, via Berlin, Vienna, Toulouse, Athens, Kassel and New York. Initiating encounters and open conversations around persistent colonial power relations, including issues of accessibility and historical awareness, the Center encourages critical questioning and invites visitors to reflect on their own weak spots. The Center does not aim to create a coherent and complete library on colonialism, because when could that ever be the case? Colonialism is unfinished business. It continues to exist in various forms. ai.en: Tatu Tuominen's four-minute video "A Near Approach to Immortality (Hercynian Forest)" on Oodi's first floor from 2 to 29 November. It explores the lost European primeval forest through Pliny's account.

events.description: Single-channel video installation, 4K, stereo sound Duration 4 min 35 s (loop) Edition of 4 + 1 AP Direction, screenplay and concept: Tatu Tuominen Assistant director, cinematography, editing and animation: Janne Laiho Sound design: Tuomas Skopa The production of the work has been supported by an AVEK project grant. Oodi Central Library 1st floor 2.11.-29.11.2026 Tatu Tuominen’s video work A Near Approach to Immortality (Hercynian Forest) explores the lost European primeval forest. The work examines what art-historical images reveal about the human relationship with the forest, both in the past and in the present. An art-historical landscape—whether based on perception or imagined—has often been presented as perfect, static, and complete. In the current ecological situation, proposing this kind of landscape seems impossible. The landscape no longer presents itself as pristine or permanent, because human activity has an impact everywhere in the world. This is why, in Tuominen’s work, landscape is in a state of becoming: imperfect, in flux, and fragmentary—as is the world around us. The historical point of departure for the work is Naturalis Historia, an encyclopedia by the Roman author and natural historian Pliny the Elder (23–79 CE). Pliny refers to the Hercynian Forest twice in Naturalis Historia. Hercynia is a mythical primeval forest that was situated beyond the borders of the Roman Empire, in the region of western Central Europe. In Pliny’s account, it emerges as an…

events.description: The paintings are meant to bring joy; the most important thing in their creation was the pleasure of creating them, and chance has often played a part in their creation. ITE means self-made (personalised) life and art created entirely by yourself; the methods emerge through the process of creation. I encourage everyone to find joy in colours in their own lives too, and to boldly step outside the box with a paintbrush or a cup of paint in hand. title.en: Réka Peurala: Not Just For The Eye

summary.en: Peurala is an award-winning photographer based in Finland. Through her work, she explores the space where commercial imagery and artistic expression intersect.

ai.en: Réka Peurala's Not Just For The Eye at the Liszt Institute in Helsinki, an exhibition that asks whether marketing photos for ads, packaging and menus can be considered art.

events.description: When people think of fine art photography, they rarely envision marketing tools. Marketing photos created for advertising, packaging, and menus are often evaluated by how efficiently they support sales, rather than their artistic value. This exhibition sheds new light on that established practice. The twelve photographs presented here were originally created within the world of commercial photography. Together, they formed the panel that was awarded the Qualified European Photographer (QEP) title. Now presented in a gallery setting, they invite you to consider a simple question: can a commercial photograph also be a work of art? Reka Peurala is an award-winning photographer, creative director, and stylist based in Finland. Through her work, she explores the space where commercial imagery, visual storytelling, and artistic expression intersect. events.description: Minun Helsinkini - Auringon taika on valokuvanäyttely, joka kutsuu katsojan kokemaan Helsingin valossa, joka kestää vain hetken. Kuusi valokuvateosta kuvaavat kaupungin maisemia auringonnousun ja auringonlaskun aikaan, jolloin tuttu ympäristö muuttuu valon myötä ainutlaatuiseksi. Näyttelyn punaisena lankana ovat valo, kotikaupunki ja henkilökohtainen suhde Helsinkiin, kaupunkiin, jonka maisemissa kuvaaja on elänyt ja liikkunut koko elämänsä. Näyttelyn tavoitteena on pysäyttää katsoja kokemaan Helsingin maisemat uudella tavalla. Valokuvien kautta tuttu kaupunki muuttuu hetkellisesti valon näyttämöksi, jossa auringonnousu ja auringonlasku tekevät jokaisesta maisemasta ainutkertaisen. Näyttely on samalla henkilökohtainen kunnianosoitus Helsingille, kaupungille, joka on ollut kuvaajan suvun kotipaikka jo viiden sukupolven ajan. "Minun Helsinkini ei ole vain paikka kartalla. Se on valo veden pinnalla, hiljainen aamu ennen kaupungin heräämistä ja ilta, jolloin aurinko maalaa tutut maisemat hetkeksi aivan uudenlaisiksi." Taiteilija tavattavissa Näyttelyn aikana kuvaaja on tavattavissa su 8.11 kello 13-14 ja su 22.11 kello 14-15 näyttelytilassa. Kävijöillä on mahdollisuus keskustella kuvaajan kanssa teosten taustoista, Helsingin kuvaamisesta sekä valon merkityksestä maisemavalokuvauksessa. Tilaisuus tarjoaa mahdollisuuden kuulla kuvien syntytarinoita ja keskustella kaupungin muuttuvista maisemista eri vuodenaikoina. *** Kallion kirjasto Viides linja 11 09 310 850 53 Facebook |…

title.en: Taidenäyttely: Mayah Holmberg - Kirkas puhdas hiljaisuus

summary.en: Mitä tapahtuu, kun maisemasta jää jäljelle vain tila, valo ja hiljaisuus? Näyttelyn teokset liikkuvat maiseman rajalla.

ai.en: "Kirkas puhdas hiljaisuus", paintings and works by Mayah Holmberg at Suomenlinna Library, about the boundary of landscape, light and silence, and the weight and lightness of space.

events.description: Mitä tapahtuu, kun maisemasta jää jäljelle vain tila, valo ja hiljaisuus? Näyttelyn teokset liikkuvat maiseman rajalla. Ne eivät kuvaa tiettyä paikkaa, vaan tilaa, jossa katse pysähtyy. Hiljaisuus on teoksissa materiaalia: se laskeutuu pinnoille, ohenee ja tiivistyy. Paino ja keveys vuorottelevat. Näyttely kutsuu katsojan hidastamaan ja kuuntelemaan, kun kaikki muu on jo liikkunut eteenpäin. Mayah Holmberg on Helsingissä asuva ja työskentelevä taiteilija, jonka teoksissa keskeistä on tilan ja havainnon suhde. Hän on tullut kuvataiteeseen tanssin ja esitystaiteen kautta, ja sama koreografinen ajattelu näkyy tämän näyttelyn teoksissa. Tyhjä tila toimii niissä taukona ja hiljaisuutena, ja muodot asettuvat suhteeseen toisiinsa kuin kehot, jotka jakavat saman tilan. Paino ja keveys eivät ole teoksissa vain kuvallisia ominaisuuksia, vaan kehollisesti koettuja tiloja. Holmbergia kiinnostaa, mikä jää jäljelle, kun liike on pysähtynyt.

summary.en: Piia Kokkarinen's oil paintings are on display at Galleria Huuto.

events.description: "Rhythm, rippling and swirls run wild in the paintings. The theme of my works is moving through space, moving towards it, leaving it behind. I look for ways to paint a world where nothing stays still, where form is constantly on its way towards another form. A large canvas gives the paint room to move, as one does not hit the edges right away. As layers of paint accumulate, tensions begin to emerge between the colors and marks. Something arises from a surprise, and sometimes it has to be searched for. At times, it is lurking in a dead end – and when the illusion of a goal disappears, the surprise may suddenly break loose. When I step into a surprise, my forward thinking disappears. I notice how thinking on autopilot puts things on a line, trying to anticipate and guess. In a surprise, the world opens up in bursts spreading in every direction. There is no knowledge of what is to come, no guarantees – only a spectrum of possibilities and a glimpse of freedom. A thorough movement bubbles to the surface, beyond the reach of words. A restless movement churns between all concepts and contexts. Alongside uncertainty and ambiguity, there is a strange certainty of existence. In the middle of unpredictability, my feelings sway between terror and exhilaration. Playfulness dances in the air." summary.en: Jussi Pyky's drawings are on display at Galleria Huuto.

events.description: "Animals move silently through the dark forest. They keep a safe distance from me. I know they are around me, even though I cannot see them. I am calm, yet alert. It is still and quiet. I feel as though I am safe. In solitude, in darkness, in silence – something emerges from within me. It feels foreign and ancient – something we would like to hide, forget or tame. Light reveals everything and makes us vulnerable. It is the absence of darkness. Perhaps that is why we want to light everything up. Darkness offers protection. Perhaps here I am safe from my other self, my daytime self. The person of culture, education, reason and light. The one who walks in the light. Tamed by oneself." Jussi Pyky (b. 1985, Tyrnävä) lives and works in Helsinki. He works with drawing and painting. He graduated from the Lahti Institute of Fine Arts in 2009 and earned a Master of Fine Arts degree from Uniarts Helsinki’s Academy of Fine Arts in 2016. Pyky has participated in several group exhibitions and held numerous solo exhibitions in Finland and abroad. He is a member of the artist cooperative Toolbox. In 2025, he received the William Thuring Prize. His works are included in the Seppo Fränti Collection at the Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art as well as in several private collections in Finland and Germany. title.en: Oliver Beer – Resonance Project: The Cave

summary.en: Oliver Beer transforms Kiasma’s top floor into a prehistoric, resonant cave.

ai.en: Oliver Beer's installation "The Cave" at Kiasma, with eight singers including Rufus Wainwright and Woodkid, filmed in a prehistoric French cave. Their voices, recorded with 16 audio channels, fill the gallery.

events.description: Lullabies, traditional songs, and voodoo melodies intertwine in this major installation at Kiasma, bringing to life the atmosphere and acoustics of a prehistoric cave. The immersive video opera is filmed in Font-de-Gaume, an archaeologically significant cave in southwestern France renowned for its hundreds of prehistoric paintings. The Cave brings together eight singers from across the globe. Musicians Rufus Wainwright, Woodkid, eee gee, Mélissa Laveaux, Hamed Sinno, Jean-Christophe Brizard, Mo’Ju, and Michiko Takahashi were each invited to perform the earliest song they could remember from childhood. Each singer performs in tune with the cave’s harmonics, their voices naturally amplified by the cave and weaving together in the gallery space into a haunting polyphony meticulously recomposed by Beer. The installation comprises 16 audio channels and eight monumental video projections arranged throughout the exhibition space. Together, the singers’ voices resonate across the gallery, evoking the experience of a cave that only a handful of people will ever have the chance to visit.

summary.en: The life of the Sámi in Helsinki is diverse and multilingual, ever-changing and living in time. It …

events.description: The life of the Sámi in Helsinki is diverse and multilingual, ever-changing and living in time. It is everyday life, work and study, and sometimes celebration. It is childhood, adolescence, adulthood and ageing. Travelling between the south and the north. It is concern for the preservation of Sámi languages and cultures, stress about the future and the next generations. The need to learn, maintain and influence. It can also be an escape from Sámi roots, a desire to blend in or hide among the masses of the city. The materials in the exhibition have been produced, selected and exhibited by Sámi people living in Helsinki. The curatorial team consists of Aimo Aikio , Laura Feodoroff , Helmi Hagelin and Mari Gauriloff . The exhibition’s designers, architect Eveliina Sarapää and graphic designer Lotta Hagelin , are also Sámi. The exhibition grew out of a documentation project in which Sámi people themselves determined what should be preserved as part of the city’s collective memory. The project highlighted themes such as connections to multiple places, passing Sámi languages and culture on to future generations and preserving them, as well as the importance of taking action in wider society to advance these issues. The exhibition also explores urban Sámi identity, as well as the history of the Sámi in the Helsinki region. Portraits by photographer Marja Helander reflect the diversity of Helsinki’s Sámi community. The exhibition also features works by Jouni S. Laiti and Sámi…

Luka (Paavo Kinnunen) ja Jarmo (Juho Milonoff) ovat toipuvia alkoholisteja, jotka ovat tavanneet AA-kokouksessa. Jarmo on vanhempi mies, joka ryhtyy hiljattain raitistuneen Lukan kummiksi ‒ tehtävänään opastaa kokemattomampaa Lukaa raittiuden tiellä. Ilman humalan suomaa estottomuutta Lukan elämä on muuttunut yksinäiseksi. Hän pelkää olevansa incel, koska ei osaa lähestyä naisia selvinpäin. Jarmon mielestä Luka tarvitsee ennen kaikkea positiivisen miehen roolimallin. Kun koittaa Lukan viidennen askeleen aika, tehtävä osoittautuu kimurantiksi. Pystyykö kumpikaan miehistä tunnustamaan pahimmat hairahduksensa täysin rehellisesti? Moraalinen itsetutkiskelu vie miehet yhä loitommaksi toisistaan. Ja kun vertaistuki muuttuu irvikuvakseen, on pohjakosketus lähempänä kuin koskaan. ai.en: "Taru hohtavasta helmestä", a family fantasy play at the Finnish National Theatre's Main Stage from 14 November to 19 December, about a gnome who takes a glowing gem into the world. It is in Finnish, for ages 7 and up.

events.description: Ikivanha Mestaritonttu asuu Satumaassa. Jo vuosisatojen ajan hän on vartioinut kuninkaan linnaa, lyhtynään salaperäinen hohtava helmi. Ajat ovat kuitenkin muuttuneet, eikä elämä Satumaassa enää ole niin kuin ennen. Kun kuningas vielä suuttuu Mestaritontulle, tämä ottaa hohtavan helmen mukaansa ja lähtee maailmalle. Matkallaan Mestaritonttu kohtaa Sammaleisen, Kyöpelinvuoren entisen hovinoidan. Yhdessä he lähtevät Suosaarelle, josta tonttu löytää itselleen uuden kodin. Mestaritonttu saa kuitenkin pian huomata, ettei noitien kanssa mikään ole sitä, miltä näyttää. summary.en: Adrienn Újházi (SR/HU) is a visual artist from Novi Sad Serbia, working at the intersection of art, science, and technology.

events.description: Unseen Artifacts examine the biological and material processes that occur in the human body and its environment beyond the limits of direct perception. These microbial and living systems largely remain invisible, becoming perceptible only when their effects manifest in larger, visible forms. Through digital documentation, material samples, and data translations, the exhibition presents living matter as an active, self-organizing agent. By combining artistic and research-based methods, Unseen Artifacts situates perception as a relational process between bodies, environments, and technologies. The exhibition not only invites the study of biological and ecological systems but also encourages reflection on the invisible interactions that shape our daily lives, health, and surroundings. Adrienn Újházi is a visual artist from Novi Sad Serbia, working at the intersection of art, science, and technology. She has participated in numerous international exhibitions, projects, and collaborations, and has received several awards and scholarships. title.en: Espoo Artists' Guild: The Value of Art

summary.en: The Espoo Artist's Guild is visiting with its group exhibition at Rantakasarmi, the historically beautiful setting of HAA Gallery in Suomenlinna.

events.description: In his 1952 book Einar Ilmoni – Kangasalan erakko (Einar Ilmoni – The Hermit of Kangasala), Håkan Gadolin describes the artist as a genius of exceptional artistic talent – despite his inherited “degenerative traits” (to quote the author). Fortunately, artists are no longer described in such harsh terms. Today, artistic talent and the vocation of an artist are generally regarded as valuable – as something that enriches society both intellectually and culturally, and sometimes economically as well. The Espoo Artists’ Guild is an association of professional artists with 54 members. In Espoo, artists work in remarkably diverse surroundings: some in the heart of the forest, others in bustling suburban neighbourhoods. One of the most important roles of a small association is to maintain connections among its members and foster a sense of community. The Espoo Artists’ Guild has sought to present the work of Espoo-based artists in distinguished exhibition venues, both locally and throughout Finland. Its geographical reach has extended in many direction: in Keuruu, Imatra, Kokemäki, Lahti and Tampere, among other places. Winter will soon arrive, and the sea will freeze over. events.description: Jiri Geller flirts with pop culture, provocation and artistic conventions. His works resemble flawless individual pieces lifted straight from a production line, yet behind every polished inch and coat of paint lies an enormous amount of labour, technical mastery and artistic vision. This extensive retrospective presents works spanning Geller’s entire career, from its early steps in the late 1990s to recent developments. The exhibition features several large-scale sculptural installations, including the God Says No escalator, The Big Time tidal wave, and Battle of the Worlds, which invites visitors into a twisted game of table football. The newest works draw inspiration from the animal kingdom, all bearing Geller’s signature touch. Several mechanically operated sculptures are also included. Geller possesses a who-gives-a-f*ck attitude and the soul of a punk rocker. He sculpts in candy colours and shades blacker than black, balancing surface and depth. His world delights and irritates, captivates and draws viewers closer, prompting reflection on questions of existence, consumer culture and craft. Kunsthalle Helsinki 21.11.2026 - 10.1.2027

Decorative candy cones were a favourite among children, and you can make your own in the museum’s chamber on two Sundays, 29 November and 20 December at 2 pm. Some of Topelius’s most cherished tales are set in Christmas and winter landscapes. These tales will be read in the museum’s chamber (in Finnish) on Saturdays 28 November, 5 December, 12 December, 19 December and 2 January, and on Sundays 27 December and 3 January, all at 2 pm. events.description: Kuvan ja sanan työpajassa Valokuvarunous, mitä se on? Valokuvarunoutta on tehty ja julkaistu 1800-luvun alkuvuosikymmenistä lähtien. Siihen verrattuna tätä kuvan ja sanan historiaa on käsitelty varsin vähän niin valokuvauksen kuin kirjallisuuden tutkimuksessa. Esimerkiksi Oxford English Dictionary ei tunne sanaa photopoetry tai photopoem. Yhtä tuntematon valokuvaruno on Kielitoimiston sanakirjalle, Tieteen termipankille ja Helsingin Sanomien arkistolle. Corkin yliopiston tutkija Michael Nott kirjoitti ensimmäisen valokuvarunouden historian Photopoetry 1845–2015. A Cricital History (2018). Nottin mukaan sanaa valokuvaruno, photopoem , käytti ensimmäisen kerran Constance Philips antologiassa Photopoems: A Group of Interpretations through Photograps (1936). Nott määrittelee valokuvarunon valokuva-tekstiksi ( photo-text ), jonka pääosat ovat runo ja valokuva. Valokuvaruno on siis runon ja valokuvan välistä työskentelyä, joka voi olla vanhojen teosten yhdistämistä, runoilijan ja valokuvaajan yhteistoimintaa tai yhden runoilija-valokuvaajan tai valokuvaaja-runoilijan työn tulos. Varsin harvoin valokuvaaja on kirjoittanut runonsa, ja yhtä usein runoilija on kuvannut teoksensa. Poikkeuksia kotimaisissa valokuvaajissa on muutama: Mikko Hietaharju, Kari Holopainen ja Ritva Kovalainen . Runoilijoista tuoreimpia esimerkkejä ovat Tekla Inarin, Maria Matinmikon ja Aki Salmelan kokoelmat. Valokuvarunoutta kehittelin blogissa Kuva ja sana 2007–2022 . title.en: Raili Tang: It All Began with Yellow

summary.en: Raili Tang’s new paintings reveal the artist’s subtle sensitivity to colour.

events.description: Raili Tang’s new paintings reveal the artist’s subtle sensitivity to colour. Her palette is at once delicate and inviting, yet also intense and unexpected, drawing the viewer in and encouraging them to pause and immerse themselves in its nuances. Tang’s paintings open windows onto different worlds, sometimes turning the gaze inwards, at other times inviting the viewer on an adventure. Curtains now frame her flower arrangements, at once concealing and sheltering them while hinting at new realms of possibility just beyond. Whereas vases played a supporting role in Tang’s earlier flower paintings, they have now assumed greater significance. Often depicted in a contrapposto stance, their curving forms evoke the human figure. At times, their shapes also draw inspiration from iconic Finnish design. Raili Tang (b. 1950) has exhibited widely in Finland and internationally. Her works are represented in several of Finland’s most prominent art collections, including those of the Museum of Contemporary Art Kiasma, the Sara Hildén Art Museum, the Wihuri and Saastamoinen Foundations, and HAM Helsinki Art Museum. Hirvimäki began his career as a painter but gained recognition in the 1980s for his public stone sculptures. In the 2000s, he moved away from his earlier style towards figurative representations of animals. His numerous public works include To Hurry Up, situated in the courtyard of Parliament House; the Mika Waltari Memorial in Helsinki; Passing By, commissioned by the University of Jyväskylä; and Fish Story, created for the New Children's Hospital in Helsinki. summary.en: The exhibition challenges conventional ways of representing architecture, shifting the focus from the building’s appearance to the networks of materials, techno

events.description: Tuomas Siitonen: New Principles (of Energy in Architecture) Architecture is often examined through space, form and visual experience. A building can appear as an independent whole, even though its existence is connected to countless material, technological, ecological and temporal relationships. Architect and graphic designer Tuomas Siitonen explores new ways of communicating these less tangible relationships and bringing them more firmly into architectural design and education. At the heart of the New Principles exhibition is the Pedagogic Kit, an experimental teaching tool and research project. Its disassembled scale model helps to understand a building as something other than a single object: an arrangement of matter and energy, whose components each have their own origins, life cycles and futures. The exhibition also examines how knowledge about architecture is produced and communicated. Drawings, images and models are not neutral tools; they shape how we interpret information and what we consider important. Together, the Pedagogic Kit and a small zine turn the gallery into an experimental learning environment. The aim is not only to communicate new knowledge, but also to question established ways of thinking. Luonnos 27.11.2026-17.1.2027 Wed-Fri 12.00-17.00 Sat-Sun 12.00-16.00 Free entry

The piece is part of Heli Valkama’s multidisciplinary working method that focuses on spatiality and visualizing ways of using space as well as habits and customs regarding it. In Extract, which premieres in Mediabox, the informativity, narrativity and spatial aspects of sound are in focus. Heli Valkama (b. 1988, Helsinki) is a visual artist-musician who works mainly with printmaking, installation and multimedia and their collision. Her multidisciplinary approach involves music and performance which continue exploring spatiality and interaction that takes place in shared space. Valkama has worked with the themes of use of space and land since 2023 while broadening her printmaking-based methods towards digital space and utilization of found material. events.description: Forum Box presents solo exhibitions by three artists: Sula Insula by Jan Anderzén, New Testament by Hemuloordi and Dustland by Inka-Maaria Jurvanen. Sula Insula consists of large-scale textile works and Joskussaaret, a record by Kemialliset Ystävät. Jan Anderzén is a collage artist originally from Nekala who has since become a Kaakinmaa local. Hemuloordi (b.1989) is a Helsinki-based sculptor who works mainly with ceramics and videos. “In my works, I deal with the contradictions of identities and how capitalism flattens and controls them. Sometimes the society we live in is so horrible and absurd, but life is also so wonderful at the same time that things somehow then unfold as art. I do a lot of self-portraits and my works are always quite psychological.” The themes of the Dustland exhibition are memories and their construction, inevitability and surrendering. The title came about while the artist was working at the Villa Karo residency. In Beninese culture sacred objects and statues play a central role, and the time and dust that has accumulated on these objects are not disturbed or cleaned away – they are accepted. Inka-Maaria Jurvanen (b.1980) is interested in time, its passage, and the representation of simultaneity and succession through two-dimensional images. Forum Box 27.11.-20.12.2026 Tue-Sun 12.00-17.00 Free entry

summary.en: A contemporary dance piece in which six performers search for the shapes of desire in the body’s subtle gestures and tensions.

ai.en: Baltic Circle and Kauri Sorvari present Forevermore, a dance work on desire and eros at Kiasma Theatre, inspired by Byung-Chul Han's The Agony of Eros. Performances run from 27 November to 5 December 2026.

events.description: Forevermore articulates the shapes, gestures, and actions of the intimate, eros and erotic at the threshold of dancing. The work portrays timeless and persistent directions of desire. The glance moves from the inner thighs, towards the iliac crest and the lower abdomen; then suddenly from the collarbones to the Cupid’s bow. Breathing pauses. Tensions build and subside, fade, repeat, and repeat again. The body of the performer attempts to locate the romantic-erotic thirst. Dance is eros, a force that pulls the self out of itself. Cupid is a naked honey thief. The performance is inspired by Byung-Chul Han’s The Agony of Eros. WORKING GROUP: Kauri Sorvari, Marlon Moilanen, Kid Kokko, Yuri Shimaoka, Ella Skoikka, Pie Kär, Pietu Wikström , Satu Kankkonen , Kristian Palmu , Emil Santtu Uuttu , Sara-Maria Heinonen , Anni Koskinen , Sofia Smeds PERFORMANCES Fri 27.11.2026 18.00 Sat 28.11.2026 15.00 Sun 29.11.2026 15.00 Tue 1.12.2026 18.00 Wed 2.12.2026 18.00 Thu 3.12.2026 18.00 Sat 5.12.2026 15.00

events.description: BabyTango combines a performance for babies with a dance session for babies and their companions. Tango is feeling, listening, a shared flow of movement, surrendering, leading and being led. At BabyTango’s core is the relationship between the baby and the parent or another significant adult. It is a state of non-verbal understanding, where movements, gestures, emotions and sounds express what is needed – when there are no common words yet. BabyTango is a session of interaction and love. summary.en: The Winter Salon creates a space for encounters and dialogue between diverse works and artistic practices.

events.description: Helsinki Contemporary rounds off the year with its Winter Salon group exhibition, which has by now become an annual tradition. It creates a space for encounters and dialogue between diverse works and artistic practices, revealing unexpected parallels and connections. The gallery’s represented artists – Emma Ainala, Roland Persson, Anna Retulainen, Emma Sarpaniemi, Kaarlo Stauffer and Aki Turunen – are joined this year by two new names: Erno Pennanen and Riikka Sormunen. In his paintings, Erno Pennanen explores what it means to be human. His subjects often include full-length portraits, everyday scenes and seemingly unremarkable objects. Alongside his exploration of the human condition, Pennanen is interested in colour and in how its combinations and contrasts can evoke distinctive spatial impressions and atmospheres. In Riikka Sormunen’s paintings, female figures, animals and still-life elements merge into dreamlike landscapes. Although rendered with meticulous attention to detail, the worlds she creates follow the logic of dreams, memory and subjective perception rather than rational realism. Her intricately detailed compositions abound in allusions to subjects ranging from ancient mythology to seventeenth-century still-life painting and Surrealism. Helsinki Contemporary 26.11.-20.12.2026 Wed-Fri 12.00-18.00 Sat-Sun 12.00-16.00 Free entry

ai.en: "Poiskatsojat" at KOM Theatre, a dark-humour documentary-style play by Susanna Kuparinen and Maria Pettersson on why Western countries look away from crises such as Gaza. It runs 7 September to 5 December, lasts 2.5 hours, and suits ages 15 and up.

events.description: Tapahtumat Gazassa järkyttävät maailmaa. Poliitikot ja media sulkevat silmänsä. Tavalliset kansalaiset kokevat voimattomuutta. Mistä kaikessa on kyse? KOM-teatterin syksyn uutuusteos on suora ja hätkähdyttävä reportaasi siitä, miksi länsimaat katsovat pois silloin, kun pitäisi puuttua. Mustan huumorin sävyttämä esitys tarjoaa faktapohjaista tietoa jokaiselle, joka on tuntenut hämmennystä maailmanpolitiikan äärellä. Ohjaaja Susanna Kuparinen on moninkertaisesti palkittu käsikirjoittaja, journalisti ja dokumenttiteatterin suunnannäyttäjä, jonka aiemmat työt ovat ravistelleet niin päättäjiä kuin katsojia. Hänen teoksissaan teatteri on tiedonvälittäjä ja kansalaiskeskustelun areena. Nyt Kuparinen tuo näyttämölle yhdessä toimittaja Maria Petterssonin ja KOM-teatterin ensemblen kanssa ehkä rohkeimman teoksensa. Siinä luhistuva maailmanjärjestys ja suomalaiset poliitikot tunkeutuvat uutisruutujen välityksellä suoraan ohjaajan olohuoneeseen. Tarkkaan journalistiseen taustatyöhön nojaava esitys tekee monimutkaisista tapahtumista ymmärrettäviä purevan farssin ja satiirin keinoin. Näyttämöllä nähdään Geoffrey Erista, Tommi Eronen, Tuuli Paju ja Hanna Raiskinmäki. events.description: KAIKEN on runoilija Petra Vallilan liikkuvaa kuvaa, ääntä ja luettua runoa yhdistelevä esitysrunoteos, joka pohjaa Vallilan runoteokseen kaiken (Poesia 2026). Kielirunoudesta innoittuva kaiken liikkuu Kalifornian viimeisimmässä kulta-ajassa, jäljittää talouspuheen väärinkäsityksiä ja keskustelee pahvilaatikkoon asettuneen näkymättömän käden kanssa työstä. Kaiken olisi voinut ajatella menevän toisinkin. Haikea teos ehdottaa yrityskielen toisinkehystelyä ja pyrkii kieltäytymään itsestäänselvyyksistä. Järjestelmän sisällä sanatkin alkavat kuulostaa surullisilta; onko tästä meille hyötyä? Esitysrunoteoksen kesto on noin 20 minuuttia, jonka jälkeen Vallila kertoo teoksesta ja sen syntyprosesseista *** Petra Vallila (s. 1983) on itähelsinkiläissyntyinen korporaatiotaustainen aikanaan Piilaaksossa työskennellyt runoilija, kirjoittaja ja esitysrunoilija, jota ajaa tahto haastaa itsestäänselvyyksiä ja neuvotella uudenlaisia tiloja. Vallilan esikoisteos ehkä (Poesia 2022) oli Helsingin Sanomien kirjallisuuspalkintoehdokkaana ja toisinkoinen kaiken (Poesia 2026) Nihil Interitin runopalkintoehdokkaana.

events.description: The tour introduces you to the famous fortress and offers interesting perspectives on the history of Finland and Northern Europe. The construction works of one of the biggest Nordic fortresses, Suomenlinna, begun in 1748. The best way to get to know the fascinating story behind the World Heritage Site of UNESCO, Suomenlinna fortress, is to join a guided tour. During the guided walking tour an authorized Suomenlinna-guide tells about the 270 years of eventful history of Suomenlinna under the rule of three different states as well as the life on the islands today. The guide will take you to the most important sights of the fortress, such as the Great Courtyard and the Dry Dock, which in its days was among the largest in the world. summary.en: Äidin täydellinen elämä. Äidin täydellisessä keittiössä.

events.description: Äitisi, Klytaimestra muuntaa Ryhmäteatterin näyttämön maternaalista voimaa uhkuvaksi, hyvin varustelluksi keittiöksi, jonka liedellä poreilee Äidin ylisukupolvinen kohtalokas bravuuri – oireileva äidinrakkaus. Minna Lundin ja työryhmän esitys kutsuu kaikille jollain tavalla tutun yksikön – perheen ja sen keskiössä ikuisesti työskentelevän Äidin – ääreen. Se on luonnottoman liioiteltu ja klaustrofobinen kuvaelma perheestä, jota ruokkii Äidin rakkaus omaan kohtaloonsa. Esitys tarkastelee Äitiä yhdessä kirjoitettuna kansansatuna – kertomuksena, jota on säilötty, toistettu ja siirretty sukupolvelta toiselle niin uskollisesti, että Äiti on jähmettynyt hengiltä. Kaikilla on villejä kuvitelmia siitä, mitä Äidin pitäisi olla ja Äitien kiroukseksi lankeaakin halu olla tuottamatta pettymystä. Näytelmä on vapaasti inspiroitunut antiikin Kreikan tragediasta Elektra, jossa Klytaimestran tytär päättää yhdessä veljensä kanssa murhata äitinsä. Elektra-myytin keskeisiä teemoja ovat kosto, pakkomielteinen suhde isään, äiti-tytär suhteiden kompleksisuus, kohtuuttomat vaatimukset sekä aggressio omaa äitiä kohtaan. Näyttämöllä näyttelijät Santtu Karvonen, Sonja Kuittinen, Minna Suuronen ja Robin Svartström sekä muusikko Mila Laine. summary.en: Red Nose Company: About The Rite of Spring – a Ritual for Four Clowns

ai.en: Red Nose Company's About The Rite of Spring is a wordless physical comedy in which four clowns explore Stravinsky's famous ballet through their own dance. Konepaja Stage, 9 September to 28 November 2026, ages 13+.

events.description: Red Nose Company: About The Rite of Spring – a Ritual for Four Clowns This performance is an unusual and surprising show inspired by Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring. The clowns dance their own choreography to music written for them. This performance is an unusual and surprising show inspired by Stravinsky’s famous Rite of Spring. Four clowns explore this great musical work and its many interpretations. They give themselves fully to the task. In the show, the clowns dance their own choreography to music written especially for them. The goal is to create a ritual that strengthens the feeling of connection — without sacrificing a young girl ever again. Also no middle aged woman have been harmed in the process. The first performance of The Rite of Spring in 1913 caused a scandal. It appeared at a time when the world was heading towards the First World War. The Rite of Spring broke many artistic traditions and has influenced Western art perhaps more than any other work. The performance is full of physical, wordless comedy. Konepaja Stage 9.9.-28.11.2026 Performances: 9.9. / 10.9. / 27.11. at 18.00 28.11. at 15.00 Tickets 19-38€ from Fienta, duration 2 h, incl. intermission Age recommendation: Adults, 13+ Language: some kind of English

summary.en: Musiikkiteatteriesitys narsismin varjossa ja valossa kasvamisesta. Groteski näyttämösatu käynnistyy, kun 30-vuotias Kertoja hakee isälleen lähestymiskieltoa.

events.description: Mainiot arvostelut saanut, monitasoinen musiikkiteatteriesitys narsismin varjossa ja valossa kasvamisesta. Rooleissa loistavat monipuoliset näyttelijät Emma-Sofia Hautala ja Emmi Nieminen. Aurinkokuninkaani kertoo perheestä, narsismista ja siitä, että toivoa on. Groteski näyttämösatu käynnistyy, kun 30-vuotias Kertoja hakee isälleen lähestymiskieltoa. Isä on kuin kuumana porottava aurinko – kaukaakin sen säteet paahtavat iholla. Oikeuden istunto saa Kertojan katsomaan isää ja omaa lapsuuttaan uudessa valossa. Millainen on matka kohti itsenäisyyttä, kun on syntynyt itsensä Aurinkokuninkaan hoviin? Narsistin lapsen mielensisäinen kamppailu muistojen ja oman itsen kanssa saa mitä mielikuvituksellisempia käänteitä, kun käsikirjoittajat Sofia Lumi ja Liila Jokelin tekevät näkymättömästä aiheesta näkyvää. Teos kantaesitettiin Vaasan kaupunginteatterissa 10.10.2025. ”Sain kokea yhden itselleni vaikuttavimmista teatterielämyksistä. Näytelmä tuli kohti, lävisti ja peilasi asioita, joihin olen etsinyt vastauksia.” – Katsojapalaute Käsikirjoitus Sofia Lumi ja Liila Jokelin Ohjaus Annuska Hannula Teatteri Avoimet Ovet 28.11.2026 18.30-20.50, sis. väliajan, esityksen jälkeen keskustelutilaisuus 20 min Liput 28,10-40,10€ Lippupisteestä Esitys on suomenkielinen, ikäsuositus 13+

summary.en: "Purge" by Sofi Oksanen brings to life Estonia under Stalin when the land must be purified of all the undesirables – no matter what the cost.

events.description: Purge brings to life Estonia under Stalin, just after the fall of the 3rd Reich, when the land must be purified – no matter what the cost – of all the undesirables; and contrasts it with the same land, the same farm, just after the fall of Communism, when another purification is taking place. In both times, the battleground is a woman’s body, and the choices that she has to make – choices so difficult she doesn’t even want to remember them. Old Aliide Truu lives in a decrepit farmhouse in Estonia. Estonia has just become independent, and she is beginning to face the consequences of her decisions 40 years ago. Into her yard stumbles the 20-year old Zara, fleeing her abusive ‘boyfriend’. Meeting Zara brings back unwanted memories – of the choices Aliide herself made that sealed her fate, and that of her sister. The women try to hold onto a normal life, one to be lived through all the destruction. Nothing protects them except their own wits: the men around them and the state machinery leave physical and psychological wounds. Purge asks Why? When will it stop? Written by Sofi Oksanen The Finn-Brit Players & Passport Productions Directed by Adrian Goldman NoName Theatre 19.11./20.11./21.11./22.11./26.11./27.11./28.11./29.11.2026 19.00-21.30 Tickets 21/16,80€ from Holvi Shopi, age recommendation 16+ Performed in English Content warning: violence, sexual violence, implied nudity

summary.en: Jarkko Mandelin’s Silence takes his signature movement-focused choreography even further, combining contemporary dance, martial arts and acrobatics.

events.description: Silence takes choreographer Jarkko Mandelin’s trademark combination of contemporary dance, acrobatics and martial arts choreography and pushes it even further. “Silence is a dance performance inspired by the performance of classical music. The dance company forms an orchestra in the tradition of classical music and does its utmost to bring the elements of the concert to life. Silence is the moment when the concerto ends, the world created disappears and the preparation for the next one begins.” Jarkko Mandelin is a contemporary dance choreographer trained in classical ballet and an internationally active instructor. He has created his own recognisable style and is particularly known as a developer of contemporary dance partnering and floor technique. Mandelin is the founder and artistic director of the Kinetic Orchestra dance company. Mandelin’s previous work (Gravity) was performed at Helsinki City Theatre for two seasons in 2021 and 2023 to sold-out audiences. events.description: Led by Finnish conductor Tarmo Peltokoski, the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra makes its Helsinki debut with German pianist Martin Helmchen, performing Saint-Saëns’ Carnival of the Animals and Wagner’s The Ring – An Orchestral Adventure. Founded in 1947 and turned professional in 1974, the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra (HK Phil) is recognised as one of Asia’s leading ensembles. In 2019, it became the first Asian orchestra to win the prestigious Gramophone Orchestra of the Year Award. Tarmo Peltokoski has rapidly established himself on the international stage. In January 2022, he was appointed Principal Guest Conductor of The Deutsche Kammerphilharmonie Bremen. He also serves as Music Director of the Orchestre National du Capitole de Toulouse, Principal Guest Conductor of Rotterdams Philharmonisch Orkest and Conductor Laureate of the Latvian National Symphony Orchestra. Peltokoski starts his tenure as Music Director of the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra in the 2026/27 season and begins a three-year residency as “Exklusivkünstler” at Konzerthaus Dortmund. Martin Helmchen has performed on the world’s most prestigious stages for two decades, established as one of today’s most sought-after pianists. His artistry is defined by exceptional tonal sensitivity and technical finesse—qualities that earned him the Gramophone Classical Music Award in 2020. ai.en: Bo Kaspers Orkester's Il Magnifico at Finlandia Hall in Helsinki, two concerts on 29 November 2026 as part of the band's 35th anniversary tour.

events.description: Bo Kaspers Orkester juhlii 35-vuotista uraansa syksyllä Helsingissä! Suomalaisyleisön rakastama Bo Kaspers Orkester saapuu syksyn 35-vuotisjuhlakiertueellaan Helsinkiin! Ruotsalaisyhtye soittaa 29.11. Finlandia-talossa kaksi konserttia, joissa se punoo upean tarinansa yhteen otsikolla Il Magnifico. "Me kuljemme käsi kädessä elämän halki, sinä ja minä", lauloi ruotsalainen iskelmälegenda Gunnar Wiklund aikanaan -- ja juuri niin Bo Kaspers Orkester on kulkenut samaa matkaa yhdessä yleisönsä kanssa jo 35 vuoden ajan. Syksyllä 2026 Bo Kaspers Orkester juhlistaa tätä yhteistä matkaa suuren juhlaesityksen merkeissä. Erityislaatuisen show'n nimi on Il Magnifico, ja se on enemmän kuin pelkkä konsertti -- kyseessä on koko elämänmittaisen uran tiivistys. Yleisö voi odottaa kuulevansa sekä rakastettuja klassikoita että täysin uutta materiaalia. Ja kuten Bo Kaspers Orkesterin tavaramerkiksi on muodostunut, kuullaan musiikki esitettynä lämmöllä, uteliaisuudella ja melankolisella hehkulla. Tarina alkoi haparoivista sävelistä kungsholmilaisessa ravintolassa ja on johtanut loppuunmyytyihin saleihin ympäri Pohjolaa. Matkan varrella Bo Kaspers Orkesterista on tullut yleisölleen kumppani niin arjessa kuin juhlassakin. Vuoden 2026 konserteissaan Bo Kaspers Orkester kokoaa yhteen koko uransa tarinan ja tarjoaa luonnollsiesti kuultavaksi myös uutta musiikkia. Olet lämpimästi tervetullut mukaan suurenmoiseen juhlaan! Bo Kaspers Orkester firar 35 år i höst i Helsingfors! Bo Kaspers orkester älskad…

events.description: Kauniaisten orkesterin syyskonsertti 29.11.2026 klo 18.00 Ovet 17.30 Väliaika - 20 min Uusi Paviljonki Läntinen koulupolku 3, Kauniainen Konsertin avaa Sibeliuksen Tapiola, sata vuotta täyttävä mestariteos, jossa suomalainen luonto saa myyttisen soinnin. Ida Mobergin Auringonnousu johdattaa uusromanttiseen valoon, josta matka jatkuu Richard Straussin Morosuksen kuuluisan monologin kautta vaikuttavaan Kuolemaan ja kirkastukseen. Straussin kerrotaan todenneen viimeisinä hetkinään, että kuolema on juuri sellainen kuin hän oli sen vuosikymmeniä aiemmin säveltänyt. title.en: Cory Henry: A Jam Good Time

summary.en: Cory Henry is coming to Helsinki with his band. He is one of the most electrifying musicians on today’s global stage blending soul, gospel, jazz, funk, and R&B.

events.description: Cory Henry is one of the most electrifying musicians on today’s global stage — a multiple GRAMMY Award winner, acclaimed composer, producer, and one of the most celebrated Hammond B-3 players of his generation. Blending soul, gospel, jazz, funk, and R&B with extraordinary ease, he has built a sound that is both deeply rooted and unmistakably his own. He first rose to international prominence as a key member of Snarky Puppy, earning three GRAMMY Awards and worldwide recognition for his virtuosity, musical instinct, and unmistakable stage presence. Since launching his solo career, Cory has become one of the most compelling live artists in contemporary music. His performances are known for their intensity, emotional depth, and fearless spontaneity — moving effortlessly between explosive groove, intimate soul, and breathtaking improvisation. No two concerts are ever the same. He has collaborated with some of the biggest names in modern music, including Kanye West, Rosalía, Stevie Wonder, Bruce Springsteen, and Imagine Dragons, while performing on some of the world’s most iconic stages and festivals. Cory Henry live is more than a concert — it is a powerful, deeply human musical experience driven by groove, emotion, and pure creative freedom. events.description: Taidetyöpajojen aarteita -näyttely Seurahuoneella Tervetuloa tutustumaan taidetyöpajojemme upeisiin tuotoksiin! Taidetyöpajojen aarteita -näyttelyssä pääset ihastelemaan Seurahuoneen luovien tekijöiden värikkäitä, kekseliäitä ja koskettavia teoksia. Näyttely kokoaa yhteen eri työpajoissa syntynyttä taidetta, jossa näkyvät tekijöiden persoonallisuus, mielikuvitus ja tekemisen ilo. Esillä on monipuolinen kokoelma teoksia, jotka kertovat tarinoita yhteisöllisyydestä, luovuudesta ja yhdessä tekemisen voimasta. Tule inspiroitumaan, löytämään omat suosikkisi ja juhlistamaan paikallista taidetta kanssamme. Näyttely on avoin kaikille ja tarjoaa elämyksiä niin taiteen ystäville kuin uteliaille ensikertalaisillekin. Tervetuloa löytämään taidetyöpajojen aarteet Seurahuoneelta! 🎨✨

title.en: Kasvuvalmennus: Asiakasymmärrys - Kuka oikeasti tarvitsee sitä, mitä yrityksesi tarjoaa?

summary.en: Kaikki eivät ole sinun asiakkaitasi. Tässä ryhmävalmennuksessa opit tunnistamaan, kenelle palvelustasi on eniten hyötyä ja mistä asiakkaasi tarpeet syntyvät.

events.description: Asiakkaat ostavat palveluita erilaisiin tarpeisiin ja tilanteisiin. Mutta tiedätkö, miksi asiakkaasi ovat ostaneet juuri sinulta? Mitä he ovat halunneet saada aikaan tai ratkaista? Entä keitä muita voisi kiinnostaa se, mitä tarjoat? Tässä valmennuksessa tarkastelet omia asiakkaitasi ja heidän tarpeitaan. Pohdit, mitä asiakkaasi oikeasti arvostavat, millaisissa tilanteissa palvelullesi syntyy tarve ja keitä muita voisit auttaa. Samalla opit erottamaan, mitä asiakkaistasi jo tiedät ja mitä vasta oletat. Tämä auttaa sinua tekemään parempia valintoja siitä, kenelle myyt ja miten tavoitat oikeat asiakkaat. Valmennuksessa pääset ymmärtämään, miksi asiakkaasi ostavat ja millaisissa tilanteissa palvelullesi syntyy tarve haastamaan käsityksiäsi siitä, kuka on sinulle oikea asiakas ja keitä sinun kannattaa tavoitella tunnistamaan, mitä asiakkaistasi vielä kannattaa selvittää ja miten voit hyödyntää tätä tietoa uusien asiakkaiden löytämisessä Valmennuksen jälkeen ymmärrät paremmin, kenelle myyt, miksi asiakkaasi ostavat ja mitä sinun kannattaa seuraavaksi selvittää löytääksesi lisää oikeita asiakkaita. Ennen valmennusta, mieti 2–3 asiakasta, jotka ovat jo ostaneet sinulta. Miksi he ostivat? Mitä he halusivat saada aikaan tai ratkaista? Millaista ryhmävalmennuksessa on? Tämä ei ole kahden tunnin luento. Valmentaja alustaa teemaa, tuo uusia näkökulmia ja käytännön työkaluja, joita pääset soveltamaan omaan yritykseesi. Työskentelemme pienessä ryhmässä, jossa pääset keskustelemaan…

title.en: Info session: Supported job search for foreign-language speakers – find your path to working life!

summary.en: Information for foreign-language clients of Helsinki Employment Services who want to work in retail, tourism, restaurant, or real estate sectors.

events.description: Do you want to start working life in Finland? Do you want to find a job that suits you? Supported Job Search for Foreign-Language Speakers is a service where you receive help with job searching and learning Finnish at work. The service is suitable for you if: you want to find a job you want to learn more about Finnish working life your Finnish language level is at least A2.1 you want to practise more Finnish you are motivated and active in looking for work you can participate in a two-week coaching program after the information session you are interested in working in retail sector. It does not matter if you do not yet have work experience in the field. In the service, you will receive personal guidance and support in a group. The goal is for you to find a job and start working. The most important thing is that you are motivated, want to learn more, and want to find a job. Come to the info session to learn more about the service! Please bring an identity document with you. summary.en: Juhani Pallasmaa Reference Library open to the public

events.description: Internationally renowned architect and professor Juhani Pallasmaa donated his personal library of approximately 12,000 volumes to the collections of the Architecture & Design Museum Helsinki in 2013. The reference library at Eteläranta 6 features around one tenth of Pallasmaa’s book collection. For the first time, visitors now have the opportunity to explore this extensive collection amassed by the architect. The selection of books offers insights into Pallasmaa’s thinking, work and interests. The library includes works that inspired him and influenced his work, reflecting Pallasmaa’s wide-ranging interest in world cultures, the arts, imagination, thought and learning. The selection also reflects the architect’s travels, exhibition projects and design work. Eteläranta 6 and its surroundings have also been taken into consideration: the selection includes literature that allows visitors to delve deeper into the architecture and history of the building, the surrounding area and Helsinki. Visitors are welcome to read and browse the books on site, but items from the reference library cannot be borrowed. A visit to the library also provides an opportunity to explore the versatile spaces of Eteläranta 6. Eteläranta 6 23.11./30.11./21.12.2026 11.1./18.1./25.1.2027 13.00-17.00 Free entry, the space is not barrier free.

events.description: Elokuvakerho Seurahuoneella Rakastatko elokuvia, hyviä tarinoita ja yhteisiä keskusteluja? Tervetuloa mukaan Seurahuoneen elokuvakerhoon! Elokuvakerho kokoontuu kerran viikossa vaihtuvien teemojen äärelle. Ohjelmassa on monipuolinen kattaus kotimaisia ja kansainvälisiä elokuvia, klassikoita, dokumentteja sekä eri kulttuureihin ja ilmiöihin liittyviä teemaesityksiä. Jokainen kokoontuminen tarjoaa mahdollisuuden eläytyä tarinoihin, saada uusia näkökulmia ja jakaa ajatuksia muiden elokuvien ystävien kanssa. Elokuvien lisäksi tärkeässä roolissa ovat kohtaamiset ja keskustelut. Katselun jälkeen voidaan vaihtaa ajatuksia elokuvan herättämistä teemoista, henkilöistä ja tunnelmista rennossa ja avoimessa ilmapiirissä. Osallistuminen ei edellytä elokuvien syvällistä tuntemusta, kiinnostus riittää. Elokuvakerho on osa Seurahuoneen yhteisöllistä toimintaa, jossa kulttuuri tuo ihmiset yhteen. Tule mukaan viihtymään, löytämään uusia suosikkeja ja kokemaan elokuvien voima yhdessä muiden kanssa. 📍 Oulunkylän Seurahuone 📅 Kerran viikossa vaihtuvin teemoin 🎬 Avoin kaikille elokuvien ystäville
